#4315. Eternal Evolution tier list - Best heroes by tier

Updated on November 4th, 2026 - Version: 1.0.556 - Added: Takeda Isshin, Soul Warrior

In Eternal Evolution, a fantasy role-playing game, you have to assemble a squad of brave heroes and fight in the eternal arena of the universe. Epic warriors from the genus of Terrans, Atlases, and Venfir will gladly join your team. To progress and win in the game, you need to know about the best heroes in Eternal Evolution.

This is why we have created an Eternal Evolution tier list of all heroes and sorted them from the best to the worst. We have created the most up-to-date tier list for the game. ETERNAL EVOLUTION TIER LIST Do not forget that our Eternal Evolution tier list is not definitive, and you can still play the characters you like, even if they are at the bottom of the list. You can always experiment with characters to see which ones work best for you, and even those that you thought were weak can bring victory if they are put in a well-balanced team.

Anyway, with that out of the way, hit the big blue button below to check out our tier list.

The characters listed at the top of our Eternal Evolution tier list are the best heroes in the game. They are very strong and have almost no disadvantages. The only task for these characters is to smash and break enemies.

Notes on Bohr Bohr is one of the best tanks available. It can throw enemy heroes and stun them. Bohr is not good at boss hunting but is great in PvP and some story mode chapters. Bohr's Primal Blood passive skill immediately gains a 15-19% shield of max HP for 6 seconds, making him a bulky contender. Notes on Emma Emma Astral Star can be considered an S-tier hunter hero, whose greatest strength lies in her bow. Destroying enemies with her bow, she delivers big, powerful hits to the target. Her strength is so great that she can easily take down enemies who have a good defense and plenty of hit points. Emma is perfect for teams that are used for farming. She will help you to get through dungeons like Deesa or the Ancient Altar very quickly. Notes on Serena Serena the Battle Angel is an S-tier list support hero. One of her strengths is single-target healing for her teammates. She is a very useful hero who will be able to keep her ally tanks alive without issue. The only small inconvenient thing about this hero is that she does not have enough AoE healing to heal an entire team.

The characters in A-tier are also very good, almost as good as the characters in the S-tier list. The reason they did not get into the list above is that the A-tier characters have minor flaws that prevent them from being even better.

Notes on Randall Randall is considered an excellent DPS character, smashing everyone and everything in his path. Despite his assassin class, many people make Randall a tank by giving him HP and armour. The reason why you should pick this hero, though, is that he buffs his and his team's attack. Similar content:

Notes on Rakkana A strong character who does good damage to enemies. At the start of the battle, he attacks the opponent's back lines and lands a few well-aimed strikes, destroying most of the back line. After creating havoc, it's much easier to get complete control of the battlefield.

The characters in the B tier are average in terms of their power. They are not bad, but they are not exactly top-notch either. These heroes are great as support or as extra force, but not as the main units on the battlefield.

Notes on Artas Artas is a pretty good character who can kill enemies of average difficulty. It is worth remembering his abilities. Artas chooses one enemy within his range and deals damage equal to 640% of his defense, putting the enemy in vengeance state for nine seconds. Enemies in this state will become main targets for Artas and have their damage decreased by 8% and each 5% HP lost will further decrease the damage of the enemy by 1% for up to 15%. Notes on Hyupnos Hyupnos is a good character who will be a great support on the battlefield. His power surge casts Arcane to suppress an enemy. The suppressed enemy cannot use any actions for three seconds, making them almost useless. During the process, it will continue to deal significant damage to the enemy, which is convenient.

This tier includes characters you should not waste your resources and time on, as they don't bring much to the battlefield. Instead, they will just take up a slot that a much more useful character could occupy.

Notes on Omar He could be described as a pretty good hero who would definitely help you in the early stages of the game. However, he is not likely to help you when you are already at the end game.

CONCLUSION This was our complete Eternal Evolution tier list. We hope that we have highlighted a lot of useful information for you and helped you choose a hero you like and that will bring you victory. Be sure to visit us again, because the tier list will be updated all the time as soon as new updates and heroes appear in the game. And make sure to give a quick glance at these Eternal Evolution codes .

#4314. Adventure of White Chord tier list - Who's your favourite heroine?

Updated on November 4th, 2026 - Version: 1.6.3

We have ranked every single heroine on our Adventure of White Chord tier list, so you know exactly who you should equip as your main hero if your goal is to destroy all the enemy waves and progress through the story stages. Of course, you can also use the heroines in the dungeons, but the difficulty of those doesn't compare to the end-game battles in the story mode.  How to pick the best hero in Adventure of White Chord Selecting one hero to help you push through the stages is pretty simple early on. You won't have much choice, but to make things easier, you should redeem the latest Adventure of White Chord codes, since you'll get some free heroes from the codes too (Mephisto)!

If wondering how to assemble your team, it's pretty simple. You want to take into account the following:

All these play an important role, so if you want to pass the stages easily, these are the elements you need to pay attention to.

In the early game, it won't matter too much, so you can just equip your strongest (strongest gear, strongest pets, strongest skills), but the more you progress, the more they will make a difference.

Adventure of White Chord tier list breakdown The tier list we've created focuses on the end-game and which heroes perform the best. There are several options, and I recommend you go for the ones in the S tier or S+ tier. As a general rule of thumb, if you happen to get Wige & Weisse, you should always use them. They're the absolute best in Adventure of White Chord, at least for now.

Now then, let's take a look at the tier list! S+ tier  |  S tier  |  A tier  |  B tier  |  C tier Original article by Cristina Mesesan. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

Wige & Weisse are the best heroes, earning them the spot at the pedestal of our Adventure of White Chord tier list. It's two heroes in one, belonging to the Aurous rarity. They have a combination of Fire and Water attacks, which also boost Water and Fire damage. Once you get them, you should equip them, even at level 1.

Elise of Light is a physical damage dealer who focuses mainly on basic attacks, but also on increasing ATK Speed, Crits, and basic attack bonus. She is great if you want a hero who can generally be good for clearing content with any pet.

Odette is one of the best AoE damage dealers of Legendary rarity. She is ranked so high because her skill boosts the Skill DMG Bonus of herself and the pets, which is a huge deal. Since she buffs pets, she basically makes your entire team a lot stronger.

Niella could be one of the best DPS heroes in Adventure of White Chord if she's upgraded. She deals a lot of flat Water damage, and her kit revolves mainly around boosting her Skill and ATK Speed.

Nidhogg is decent because of her Physical trait, which is overall good. She doesn't have any elements, but she has increased Skill Damage Bonus, which scales really well into the late game.

Surtur is similar to Nidhogg, except that she belongs to the Fire element. She has insane Attack Speed, but also applies Burn Points to enemies, which deal additional damage.

Ankh deals Wind damage, and she can boost her Wind DMG Bonus. Her basic attacks deal additional Wind damage, and a lot more Wind damage if she deals a Crit. She also has pretty low Cooldowns once she is upgraded.

Yang Yuhuan relies on her Fire basic attacks to do the work. She can boost her Basic ATK DMG Bonus, but also her ATK Speed and Fire DMG Bonus. She deals more damage the lower her HP goes, which can be good in certain scenarios (mainly dungeons).

Cordelia is one of the very few heroes with a skill that is more defensive than offensive. She can gain a shield and regen some of her HP, which is also good situationally. She's not ideal for the story mode, but for some dungeons, she can be really useful.

Mahou Shoujo is a Mythic hero who can inflict Weathering Points on the enemy. She is available for free to new players, which is useful, especially in the early game. She is quite strong towards early-mid game, but not ideal for the later stages.

Odile and Pamina are two Epics, and the only Epics we have right now. Odile is Water-type, while Pamina is Physical, but both of them are pretty average (or rather, below average) when it comes to how good they are in end-game scenarios.

Odile is available for free for just logging in and doing your dailies for 7 days, so she is a good hero to use until you have something better (preferably from the S or S+ tier).

All the characters in the last section of our Adventure of White Chord tier list are okay in the early game until you get something better, but they tend to fall off ever so slightly towards the end-game. They are not that rare (they are mainly Mythic or Rare), which means their basic stats are a lot lower than some of the Legendaries'.

I recommend you only use them until you get something better, since you have no chances of getting Legendaries until you upgrade your gachas to higher levels.

#4313. d4v41 and Jinggg leave Paper Rex after 7th–8th Champions finish, Pacific place secure

Paper Rex has parted with captain d4v41 and Jinggg, two Masters Toronto winners, after an early exit at Champions 2026. With its VCT Pacific partner place secure, the Singapore organisation is rebuilding by choice as free agency opens to every region.

Paper Rex has broken up the core of its VALORANT roster. The Singapore organisation is parting with its captain and one of its best-known players as the 2027 season approaches. d4v41 had been with Paper Rex since its founding in 2020. He played first on its CS:GO roster, then moved with the team to VALORANT. Jinggg joined on 28 September 2021.

Neither player has named a destination. In the farewell video Paper Rex released, d4v41 said he was moving to a new team. Jinggg wrote on X that he was excited about what comes next. d4v41 also asked fans to keep supporting the organisation after both have gone.

The split follows a season that faded at the end. Paper Rex were runners-up at both Masters Santiago and Masters London earlier in 2026. At Champions in Shanghai, they lost 2-0 to LOUD in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 7 October. A 2-1 defeat to T1 in lower-bracket round one ended their run on 9 October. The event carried a $2,250,000 prize pool. LOUD went on to beat Team Vitality in the final.

The pair leave with a long record together. Jinggg helped Paper Rex to second place at Masters Copenhagen 2022. He was also part of the run to the Champions 2023 final, where the team were runners-up. Liquipedia lists both players in the line-up that won VCT 2025 Masters Toronto.

The changes are not forced by the league. The organisation is owned by IMPLS Entertainment Pte Ltd. Riot has cut the number of partner teams in each region from ten to eight for 2027–28. That leaves 32 across the four regions.

The Pacific format rewards that security. The eight partners receive seeded places at Kickoff in January 2027. Four further places go to teams that come through open qualifiers. Paper Rex can therefore reshape its roster without needing to qualify.

Two Masters winners on the open market could matter well beyond the Pacific. EMEA’s eight partners for 2027 are Fnatic, BBL Esports, FUT Esports, Team Heretics, Team Liquid, Gentle Mates, Karmine Corp and Team Vitality. Under Riot’s open qualifier rules, most regions require three of a team’s five players to come from that region. Teams must also keep three of five players between events to carry their progress forward. Those limits will frame how far any club can rebuild around new signings.

Khalish has been part of Paper Rex since our founding in 2020, starting first on our CS:GO Roster and transitioning with the team to VALORANT. We'll always remember the laughs, the op shots, and every achievement through the years.

From everyone at Paper Rex, we wish @d4v41vlr… pic.twitter.com/UgWKD4QfOj

Later in November, open qualifiers get under way. The season’s first Masters event follows in February 2027.

#4311. Fragmentary Order Looks Like Sci-Fi Escape from Tarkov, And You Can Play It This Year

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

If you've ever wondered what Escape from Tarkov would look like if its brutal firefights took place somewhere beyond Earth, Nikita Buyanov might have just the answer. The game director behind the popular hardcore shooter has finally offered a proper look at his next project, and it seems he's not planning to make things any easier for players.

Called Fragmentary Order, the upcoming sci-fi tactical shooter just received its first gameplay reveal, featuring an impressive 14 minutes of in-engine footage. And if you're curious to see what Buyanov has been working on, you can watch the full gameplay reveal on YouTube!

Escape From Tarkov's creator reveals that his upcoming game is 'almost there.'

Set across the Solar System in 2251, Fragmentary Order imagines a future where warfare has become an outsourced business. So, instead of putting their own lives on the line, players control remotely operated clones known as RepEnts, which are deployed across large combat zones to carry out all sorts of dangerous missions.

Interestingly, losing one of these clones isn't necessarily the end of the road. In this world, death is simply another business expense, but that doesn't mean players can afford to be careless. The game features large-scale environments, changing environmental conditions, vehicles, drones, and advanced technological systems, with squads of up to four players expected to coordinate their operations.

If you've ever wondered what Escape from Tarkov would look like if its brutal firefights took place somewhere beyond Earth, Nikita Buyanov might have just the answer.

Buyanov is also taking a more grounded approach to its sci-fi setting (as you should expect from the same mind that created Escape From Tarkov). Rather than relying on futuristic gimmicks like wall-hacks, the upcoming hardcore shooter features electromagnetic sensors that can expose players' positions, meaning every encounter requires careful planning and an understanding of the battlefield. In other words, running around without thinking twice probably won't get you very far!

Battlestate Games boss Nikita Buyanov opens up about his creative vision for his upcoming game, Fragmentary Order.

Alongside the gameplay reveal, Buyanov also announced “Prime Batch”, a paid program that gives players access to the game's upcoming closed testing sessions. So yes, some dedicated fans won't have to wait until the game's full release to get their hands on it, as closed testing sessions are expected to begin later this year.

There are two available tiers: Candidate ($44.99), which includes access to alpha sessions and major technical playtests, and Founder ($79.99), which adds earlier access to experimental builds, roadmap updates, and a private community with direct developer access. The first closed alpha wave is planned for later this year, and you can check out more about it on this page.

For now, Fragmentary Order doesn't have a confirmed release date, but its first gameplay showcase has certainly given fans plenty to discuss. If Buyanov manages to capture the same long-term appeal that made Escape from Tarkov so popular while introducing a compelling sci-fi setting, his next project could be one worth keeping an eye on.

Fragmentary Order is a next-generation multiplayer combat tactical simulator.

#4310. The Blood Of Dawnwalker Update 1.1 Adds Quality Of Life Improvements, Boosts Performance, and Adds Pettable Animals

We've been enjoying The Blood of Dawnwalker, one of the year's biggest games, but its release was a little rough around the edges. It took a lot of feedback from fans for developer Rebel Wolves to prioritize higher framerates at launch for consoles, but even then, the game certainly struggled at times on my PlayStation 5. Today, the game's first major update drops, and it aims to smooth some of those performance issues and introduce a few quality-of-life features.

The trailer above highlights combat-specific improvements, like improved targeting and animations, and a less restrictive camera. Rebel Wolves is also lowering the health of wolves and boars, who previously remained tanky even into the later hours of the game, and it should be easier to disengage from combat, should you choose to do so. For casual players, there's a new difficulty mode; what was previously "Story" mode has been renamed "Forgiving," while the new version of "Story" mode adds additional combat assists.

Rebel Wolves has also added some new features outside of combat. A new Daught of Mind Rebirth potion allows you to respec your skill tree, re-allocating time and skill points spent to switch up your build. You can also increase the size of subtitles (an option I'm always grateful for) and pet dogs and cats. Finally, the Shadowstep and Planeshift systems should be more responsive now – here's hoping I have an easier time teleporting onto rooftops instead of the wall right below them.

Those are the major, most visible highlights, but players can view the full patch notes here to see the hundreds of other minor improvements that aim to squash bugs, reduce crashes, and improve stability.

For more on The Blood of Dawnwalker, you can check out our review, in which our reviewer admires the swings the developers took, even though they don't always pay off. You can also check out our coverage hub for our issue devoted to The Blood of Dawnwalker, including interviews with its ex-Witcher development team.

Use the Anime Vanguards tier list to see how the new units rank and how the old ones hold up after the newest update.

Updated on November 4th, 2026  Anime Vanguards has received its latest major update that brings a fresh story, new gameplay elements, and - most importantly - some brand new units. You can now add more powerful units to your decks, mostly inspired by the latest anime sensations like Jujutsu Kaisen, Demon Slayer, and the recent hit Dandadan.

Since most of the new units are of the Mythic and Legendary rarity, things have changed at the top of the pyramid. While some old units have stood their ground, fresh faces have replaced others.

In our Anime Vanguards tier list, you can see exactly how the new units rank against the old ones. But first, take a moment and rake in some freebies by redeeming the latest Anime Vanguards codes.

Once you’ve redeemed every code, click on the big blue button to see the rankings of each character in the game.

If you think that Blade Dancer Cha-In is strong, wait until you get one of these and see what OP units really are!

Apart from the Legendary Super Brolzi, every other unit in the SS tier is an evolved version. That says a lot about the power levels of Legendary Super Brolzi and why it’s a meta unit. Then you have the two best sorcerers, Gujo and Tuji, evolving to new heights. Tuji gets a damage buff and a brand new passive while Gujo - after his Infinity evolution - gets a damage boost, a freeze passive, and an SPA deduction.

Similarly, the other evolved versions - Tengon (Flashiness), Igros (Elite Knight), Vogito Super (Awakened), and Alocard (Vampire Knight) - also gain certain boosts and passives that make them worthy of the SS tier. Evolving them is a costly affair and requires a lot of grind, but it’s totally worth it.

The unit that you really want right now is Divalo (Requiem) - the strongest and rarest unit in the game. From slowing down enemies to dealing 4-figure damage at base level, this guy has it all!

The S-tier is full of demoted units that were replaced by new blood! However, they are still formidable, making great potential additions to your team, especially units like Akazo (Destructive) and Song Jinwu (Monarch). Even after getting nerfed, they remain strong enough to destroy wave after wave of enemy units single-handedly.

If you think the evolutions are too costly, you can get by pretty well using the units in tier A. It’s full of units that are relatively easy to evolve and base versions that are strong enough to build upon.

The Boogie ability of Todu is handy enough, but the evolved Todu (Unleashed) brings a massive damage boost and SPA decrease, which gets him into the A tier. Other evolved versions in this tier also have impressive stats. Sosuke (Storm) can Stun enemies and deal double the damage of the Sosuke (Hebi) version. Similarly, Julias (Eisplosion) gets massive damage and RNG. Moreover, every attack freezes the enemies, a handy little passive in every game mode.

Both the base and evolved versions of Obita end up in the same tier because the stats and performance remain pretty much the same. Obita (Awakened) looks a lot cooler, though.

The B-tier of our Anime Vanguards tier list has the highest population because average units are aplenty.

Some Epic units like Alligator, Blossom, and Kinnua have also ended up in our B tier, and that’s because they are the best ones out of the lot. On the other hand, we also have some Legendary units like Itochi, Kinaru, Vogita Super, and the brand-new Nobaba that fail to meet expectations.

The worst mythical character in the game, in my opinion, Sasuke (Hebi) is also a B-tier resident along with Noruto (Six Tales) and Obita. No, I don’t hate Naruto characters - maybe Starburst does.

No matter what unit you pick from this list, treat it as expendable and don’t spend too many resources on any of these. It's just not worth it.

While there are some famous names on here, the game doesn’t quite do them justice.

Demon Slayer fans would have been quite excited to see Nazuka coming to Anime Vanguards. However, it didn’t go according to plan. Hopefully, we get an evolution in the coming updates that unleashes the true potential of this demon.

Similarly, other units like Sosuke and Noruto are no better. The only difference is that some of these units can be evolved into stronger versions, while others are left for dead once the going gets tough. None of the units at the bottom of our Anime Vanguards tier list are worth going after. However, you might have to make do with a few of these for their low deployment cost.

#4308. TYLOO’s Lisbon forfeit dents Singapore Major hopes as 100 Thieves edge out fnatic

TYLOO's withdrawal from a HyperX Retake Season 13 quarter-final in Lisbon has left their PGL Major Singapore invite in doubt on cutoff day. In Europe, fnatic are shut out of the last CS2 Major of 2026 after the final weekend's results went against them.

One walkover in Lisbon looks set to decide Asia’s line-up for the PGL Major Singapore.

Neither TYLOO nor Lynn Vision is expected to play again before the cutoff. That leaves the Asian race effectively over.

The Lisbon event was a Valve Tier 2 tournament run by Hyped and PEW PEW. It ran from 29 October to 1 November with 13 teams and a prize pool of €12,187.50. Groups were GSL-format best-of-threes, followed by single-elimination best-of-three playoffs. TYLOO are listed in joint fifth to eighth place.

IEM Beijing is a far bigger draw on paper. ESL is staging it from 2 to 8 November at the Bloomage Biotech Biohyalux ECM Arena. It is S-Tier and Valve Tier 1, with 16 teams playing for $1,250,000.

TYLOO were not alone in stepping away from Lisbon. Natus Vincere also withdrew, and the organisers cited the same Beijing commitment for both teams. For NAVI, the withdrawal leaves their Major chances unchanged. They had until 19 October to pull out, but were still registered after that deadline. The Lisbon event overlapped with PGL Masters Bucharest and finished less than a day before IEM Beijing began.

After the win over 9z, the team’s points already looked sufficient, according to TYLOO coach WeiJie ‘zhokiNg’ Zhong. By that stage, they had no choice but to play the Retake event. Before IEM Beijing, he also spoke about Dongkai ‘Jee’ Ji’s recovery and the problems the team has faced this season.

Europe holds 18 of the 32 Singapore invitations, one more than it had at Cologne. The six highest-ranked eligible European teams in the 2 November standings go straight into Stage 3.

The fight for the final European spot went to the last weekend. 100 Thieves beat Wildcard 2-0 in Sunday’s FiRe Last Chance final, and the European VRS now places them 18th. Elsewhere, HOTU finished second at GLuck Moscow Cyber Games.

That was bad news for fnatic. Before the final, they sat 18th in Europe with no matches left. Their only route in was a 100 Thieves defeat and recalculated standings falling their way. Neither happened.

【TYLOO Esports Club CS2 Division – IEM Beijing Roster Announcement】

TYLOO's roster for IEM Beijing 2026 is as follows:

【Players】IGL: Mercury (Wang Jingxiang)Rifler: Zero (Su Jingshen)Rifler: JamYoung (Yang Yi)Rifler: Moseyuh (Chen Qianhao)AWPer: Jee (Ji Dongkai)… pic.twitter.com/ijLS9dohdk

Moscow Cyber Games still produced a Major qualifier. Winners 1win earned a Stage 2 invitation to Singapore.

PGL set 2 November as the cutoff so the most recent results would shape the field. The weekend’s results did exactly that. The Singapore Major runs from 24 November to 13 December, with 32 teams and $1,250,000 in prize money.

#4307. Dispatch's Anniversary Update Brings Commentary Track, Storyboard Mode, And Mobile Port

Dispatch, a superhero-themed workplace comedy from last year, celebrates its one-year anniversary today. While it was released episodically, the first batch dropped on October 22. It was received well, with strong performances from a star-studded cast (including Breaking Bad star Aaron Paul) and filled a niche left vacant by Telltale Games' absence from the gaming world in recent years. Today, developer AdHoc announced a batch of anniversary content, and some of it drops today.

First, there's a new way to play Dispatch: storyboard mode. This option lets you play through the whole experience using the original animatics – rough placeholder sketches that the artists used to sync images up to the voice-over. It's a fun behind-the-scenes look at the game's development that we don't get very often. In that same vein, the cast and crew recorded DVD-style commentary tracks to play over the game, making jokes and sharing insight into the development process. A press release says there are over 16 hours of commentary from the game's development team (like art director Derek Stratton and creative directors Dennis Lenart and Nick Herman) as well as some of the cast, including Aaron Paul, Laura Bailey, and Erin Yvette.

Storyboard and Commentary modes are included in the game's deluxe edition, which you can upgrade to for $10.99. Both modes are available today.

If you haven't played the game yet, AdHoc has announced a new way to do so; Dispatch is coming to mobile platforms on December 9. It's been rebuilt to support touch controls and vertical play, and it will be available on iOS and Android. You can even play the first half of the game for free – the first four episodes are included, but you'll need to pay $19.99 to play the rest.

Finally, AdHoc announced new merch, including a book created alongside publisher Lost in Cult called Dispatch: Design Works, which is both an art book and a "making-of" book. There's also a live game soundtrack concert in Los Angeles featuring Thot Squad, Bershy, Primer, Caroline Kingsbury, Fartbarf, and Dispatch composer Andrew Arcadi with the SDN Company Band. It will be held at Avalon Hollywood on December 3, but it won't be livestreamed, so you'll need to grab a ticket to see the event. The press release states that people who signed up for updates from adhocstudio.com will be the first in line to purchase tickets.

#4306. Tomorrow's Battlefield 6 patch somehow makes jets more useless, improves armor bar visibility in Redsec

The first Battlefield 6 patch of the year is almost here, bringing a smattering of changes, including one that doesn't quite make sense.

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

The patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

The other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

Read on below for the 1.1.3.5 change log.

#4304. Jordan Esports Federation signs MoU with King Hussein Business Park to host more events

Priya Venkatesh has been following the money in esports since before brand deals were considered legitimate marketing. She got pulled into the scene through competitive fighting games and eventually found herself more interested in the contracts and partnerships behind the tournaments than the matches themselves. These days she focuses on how brands navigate esports sponsorships, where the smart money is going, and which deals are actually built to last versus the ones that look good in a press release.

The Jordan Esports Federation (JEF) has signed a memorandum of understanding with King Hussein Business Park (KHBP) in Amman, giving the national body a formal framework to stage more tournaments and events at the site it already calls home.

KHBP announced the deal on Sunday in a statement published on its website. Prince Omar bin Faisal, who is President of the JEF, attended the signing.

Under the MoU, the federation and the business park will jointly host and organise specialised competitions on the KHBP campus. They will also receive the international delegations and official guests that travel to those events. Beyond the competitive side, the two organisations plan to cooperate on media and marketing, look at shared education, training and community projects, and swap knowledge and expertise.

Neither party has disclosed financial terms or the length of the agreement.

KHBP CEO Eng. Ammar Ezzeddin presented the MoU as part of the park’s wider ambitions. “This partnership builds on our ongoing efforts to create an enabling environment for institutions, initiatives and high-potential sectors, and to establish KHBP as a hub for innovation and technology,” he said.

He added: “We look forward to helping the sector thrive and to hosting more tournaments and events that put Jordanian talent in the spotlight and raise the Kingdom’s profile in this field.”

JEF Vice President Hazem Bawab focused on the competitive and grassroots goals. “This partnership is a significant step in our drive to develop the esports industry in Jordan and elevate the standard of local, regional and international competitions and activities,” he said.

Bawab continued: “We look forward to drawing on the setup and capabilities that KHBP offers to scale our work, nurture young talent and launch joint programmes that help the industry grow and encourage greater participation.”

The deal formalises a relationship that already exists on the ground. According to The Esports Radar, the JEF, which is the government recognised regulator for esports in the country, is based at the park in West Amman.

A lot of that work happens at THE ARC, the arena and gaming dome inside the park. The same report lists past events there including the fourth Arab Esports League, a Women’s Esports Championship and Red Bull Login, which doubled as Jordan’s national final stage in Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2. The venue is also an incubation centre supported by the federation and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, and runs training camps for players hoping to turn professional.

KHBP has been a destination for esports investment for some time. In 2024, lounge operator True Gamers announced plans for an esports venue in Jordan at the business park, a project in which its CPO publicly thanked the JEF and Prince Omar.

The timing also puts Amman in the industry spotlight. PocketGamer.biz points out that Pocket Gamer Connects Jordan takes place on 7 and 8 November, bringing many of the region’s games industry stakeholders to the city later this week.

#4303. Tenebris Somnia Review – A Hair-Raising And Entertaining Throwback

Tenebris Somnia channels the old-school appeal of classic point-and-click adventures, survival horror, and full-motion-video (FMV) experiences, then smartly modernizes them to create a creepy, entertaining experience. Surviving the twisted threats of a demonic dream world is a tightly packed adventure that rewards you with what’s essentially an impressive indie horror film peppered throughout. It’s a nightmare you may not want to wake up from.

The blend of live-action and in-game storytelling works well in Tenebris Somina’s adventure, which begins when protagonist Julia visits the apartment of her filmmaker ex-boyfriend, Ivan, after suffering recurring nightmares of him being massacred by monsters. What begins as a well-meaning check-in on his status spirals down an unsettling rabbit hole when Julia’s worst fears are realized and then some. The dialogue-free tale presents a scary but fascinating exploration of obsession, both in art and in romance, that constantly delivers surprising, and at times upsetting, revelations during its eight-hour runtime. While Tenebris Somnia sometimes leans a little too far into “tell, don’t show” territory when explaining the cool lore of its supernatural threats, I never felt lost or confused about the wild things that regularly unfold on screen.

FMV experiences are nothing new, but Tenebris Somnia’s live-action scenes are a highlight. They’re well shot, sport impressively gruesome practical effects, and even present visual clues that make them important to gameplay. These scenes are additive, never taking too much time away from the in-game action, and they feel well placed to elicit the strongest emotional response. I also appreciate how the live scenes fit thematically, as much of Tenebris Somnia’s tale centers on a horror film shot by Ivan and Julia that significantly impacted their former relationship; at times, it’s like watching a movie about the movie. While I enjoy smaller moments, like opening a door to trigger a live-action jump scare, the filmmaking succeeds in selling Julia's emotions and the cast's reactions. Seeing real fear, concern, and determination in Julia’s eyes as she navigates a dreamworld made up of Ivan’s memories helped endear me to what would otherwise be a featureless pixel sprite.

Gameplay may look unimpressive due to its old-school adventure game presentation, but Tenebris Somnia’s spin on familiar survival-horror mechanics hits the right notes. Taking place entirely within a dreamlike version of a four-story apartment building, you’ll traverse floors collecting and combining objects and deciphering clues to solve well-crafted puzzles. I’m impressed by how well the game’s puzzles make the most of its limited graphical presentation, including clever scenarios involving mirror/screen reflections I won’t spoil, and how consistently creative they are. One devious exercise even utilizes the game’s limited save points as an unexpected resource in a way that changes how you approach your adventure going forward. No matter how strange puzzles become, they are never opaque, requiring just enough out-of-the-box thinking to make me feel smart when I connect the dots.

Battling grotesque monsters (which, naturally, look even creepier in live-action) also feels good, with melee and gunplay sporting deliberate animations reminiscent of classic adventure games without feeling mechanically clunky. Taking on multiple enemies by swinging a pipe or blowing them away with a shotgun feels better than it looks, and the most intense encounters end just as they approach the line of becoming overwhelming.

Boss battles, perhaps most unexpectedly for a largely puzzle-focused adventure, are fun and distinct from each other, be it wave-based bouts against small gremlin-like foes, protecting a fragile effigy of yourself from a parade of demented house servants, or battling literal mirror images of a tentacled flesh monster the Resident Evil series would be proud to claim. Managing limited ammo and health strikes a good balance of feeling tense but not oppressive. Playing conservatively is rewarding, as few non-boss threats need to be engaged if you can evade them well enough. But when I did find myself down to my last bullet or on the verge of death, Tenebris Somnia lets you feel the pinch just long enough before dropping a box of bullets or a health vial at the right moment.

Tenebris Somnia mines the enjoyable nostalgia of playing the horror games of yesteryear without feeling dated in the worst way. Weaving a solid indie horror film adds to the experience rather than feeling like a gimmick. The result is a captivating, well-executed survival-horror romp that maintains a hair-raising atmosphere with a fraction of the pixels of other genre giants.

Feel free to use the links below to check out a specific tier you're interested in! S+ tier  |  S tier  |  A tier  |  B tier  |  C tier Original article by Cristina Mesesan. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

Superman is as strong as you would expect him to be. A tank that can attack every character on the enemy team and add two stacks of burn. Whenever the stacks detonate, he gains physical damage reduction, on top of the damage reduction he already has. When he takes fatal damage, he does the most Superman thing, gaining immunity for one round. Once the round ends, he heals for 10% of his HP. Lex Luthor

Lex is a super villain tank who can support his team in various ways. He can shield his allies and remove their debuffs, but can also rally them to battle by granting them extra basic attacks. That's why he has such a high position on our DC Worlds Collide tier list. Wonder Woman

Wonder Woman is an AoE damage hero who buffs her allies by granting them crit damage bonuses. Not only that, but Wonder Woman can inflict silence and stun her enemies.

Flash is a multi-target damage hero who can knock back his enemies' action bar. If he takes fatal damage while there are no other allies on the field, Flash can turn back time and heal himself, remove every debuff, plus gain ultimate points. Batman

Batman attacks an enemy multiple times, dealing physical damage while applying a stack of Armor Break per hit. He can take down tanky enemies fast. Constantine

Constantine is one of the very best true AoE damage units. He can be very effective in pretty much any team comp, as he doesn't need synergies to deal tons of damage. Starfire

Starfire can deal high amounts of damage to an enemy row and also dispel one of their buffs. At the same time, she gets increased damage when attacking the front row and gets an armor penetration buff that lasts for two rounds. Nightwing

Nightwing is an agility tank that can be a part of pretty much any team. He has high block chances to go along with the ability to attack and stun the enemy's highest attack unit, making him one of the best in his role. Zatanna

Zatanna is an excellent support unit who can be a part of many team comps. She can attack the enemy's front row and apply the Armor Break status that lasts until the end of the battle. She also provides Strong Attack and Frantic buffs to her allies, plus life-steal.On top of that, her ultimate only costs two energy.

Green Arrow can attack every enemy unit with his skill, Rain of Arrows, and he's very good at clearing the board. Whenever an enemy dies, he gains another round. Superboy

There will be times when Superboy will drive you crazy due to the nature of his kit. But he's an interesting character, and his tactical resonance ability makes him a staple in any kind of burn team. Red Hood

Jason Todd, aka Red Hood, is a character that has the potential to do very high, single-target physical damage. His ultimate move, Resurrection, will bring him back to life after two rounds. Gorilla Grodd

Grodd is a tank that scales off enemies' debuffs. He can apply various negative status effects with his attacks, but also whenever he's attacked. Bizarro

Bizarro shares an amount of damage with an ally he links, while at the same time providing damage reduction and a small amount of healing. He possesses an AoE ability that weakens every enemy unit for two rounds, and can apply Frostbite stacks and Freeze status. Kid Flash

Kid Flash is an amazing healer who also provides various defensive buffs to his allies. He's tactical resonance buffs his healing ability even more.

There's not a lot Penguin can't do. He can attack the enemy back line and heal for a percentage of his max HP. His Umbrella Shield increases his own defense while at the same time providing damage reduction to his back row allies. His versatility is what makes him shine. Bane

A tank that can attack every enemy and apply negative effects on them - how about that? His self-heal is very strong, and at maximum rank, his ultimate costs no points. Works best with characters that can heal him.

As her name suggests, she's all about inflicting poison on her enemies. The more stacks of poison they have, the more damage she will do, and she can do a lot with the right synergies. Robin

Little Damian Wayne, aka Robin, is a hero who can deal huge amounts of damage to the enemy. He charges the back row to attack a single target three times while he applies a stack of bleed whenever he does damage. His tactical resonance requirements are not hard to meet.

#4301. KRÜ Blaze win Game Changers Championship from lower bracket, ending Gentle Mates’ unbeaten run

KRÜ Blaze came through the lower bracket to beat Europe's Gentle Mates GC over five maps in São Paulo, giving LATAM its first Game Changers Championship title. They are also the last winners of the standalone event, as next year's final moves to Champions.

KRÜ Blaze are the 2026 VALORANT Game Changers Championship winners. They edged Gentle Mates GC 3-2 at the Riot Games Arena in São Paulo on 1 November. No Latin American team had lifted the title before. No team had ever won it from the lower bracket either.

The event ran from 22 October, with 10 teams competing. Gentle Mates earned US$100,000 as runners-up. Shopify Rebellion Gold took US$70,000 for third place and MIBR GC US$50,000 for fourth.

KRÜ took the long route. They beat Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 23 October. A 2-0 loss to Shopify Rebellion Gold on 27 October then dropped them into the lower bracket. They answered with clean sweeps of Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC. On 31 October they beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 3-1 in the best-of-five lower-bracket final.

The grand final swung back and forth. Gentle Mates took Haven 13-5 before KRÜ levelled on Abyss by the same score. KRÜ led the third map 10-2 at half-time. Gentle Mates fought back, but KRÜ closed it out 14-12 in overtime. Gentle Mates then won Split 13-8 to force a decider. KRÜ led 11-5 on Ascent and won it by the same margin as Split.

Liquipedia named KRÜ’s Argentine player tok1o as the event’s MVP. Brazilian teammates antG and none became the first Brazilians to win an international tournament held in São Paulo.

The result breaks a pattern. Before 2026 the title went to G2 Gozen for Europe in 2022, Shopify Rebellion for North America in 2023 and 2024, and Team Liquid Brazil in 2025. KRÜ’s own record at the event had improved steadily. They finished 7th–8th in 2022 and 5th–6th in each of the next two years. Last year they came fourth.

For European fans, it was a painful near miss. Gentle Mates GC arrived as EMEA’s top seed on circuit points. The team had not lost a series in São Paulo before the final, according to Esports News UK.

It capped a strong debut season in the circuit. Gentle Mates won EMEA Stage 1 by sweeping G2 Gozen 3-0 on 22 February. They lost the Stage 2 final to SK Nebula on 24 May without winning a map. On 30 August they lost the Stage 3 final to G2 Gozen in a fifth map. Silver in São Paulo leaves them with one title from four finals this year.

After a lower bracket run in São Paulo, the LATAM squad claimed the #VCTGameChangers Championship trophy! pic.twitter.com/YeSeb10TZc

— VCT Pacific (@vctpacific) November 1, 2026

The São Paulo final also closes a format. KRÜ are the last team to lift the trophy at a separate event of its own. For the first time, the Game Changers Championship will finish at Champions. Under Riot’s 2027 plan, non-partner teams that qualify for the Game Changers Championship will receive an extra US0,000 incentive. VALORANT Champions 2027 is scheduled for 16 September to 10 October in Austin.

#4300. Heartopia surprise launches on Steam and shockingly, everyone seems to be happy

Heartopia players didn't actually end up having to wait too long to play the game on Steam, which is certainly not what anyone expected.

Heartopia has officially arrived on Steam, only a little over a week after it launched on iOS and Android. When the game’s release date was announced back in December, developer XD said it was pushing back the Steam release without offering any hints about how long the delay was going to be.

While the game can be played on PC through TapTap, the developer’s own emulator, many had been anticipating the Steam launch. So you can imagine that when the free-to-play life sim game surprisingly showed up on Valve’s platform on Saturday, there were a lot of happy people.

Heartopia’s Steam release has, much like mobile launch, been a success. We do know that the game reached the number one spot across app stores in over 50 countries, and though the Steam numbers may not be as record-breaking, everything is looking pretty good.

The game peaked at a decent 28,815 concurrent players (via SteamDB) on Steam one day after it launched, and considering how sticky it has been with the majority of those players so far - and the fact the launch itself was a surprise - there’s every chance those figures will improve over the course of this week as it picks up momentum.

Steam user reviews have similarly been quite positive, with the overall rating currently sitting at Mostly Positive, based on over 1,400 reviews.

You’re still need either a Google, Facebook, or Apple account to log into the game, same as you would on mobile. The Steam version does support cross-play with other platforms, so you’ll be able to play with your friends on mobile.

We’ve been playing a lot of Heartopia ourselves, and have been updating and expanding our guides. If you’re looking to get started, such as with how to add and play with friends, how to regain Energy, and how to unlock home plots, our guides offer the best place to start.

Once you’re past the initial hump, you’ll probably be looking for where to find things like mushrooms, bugs, fish, and birds, so definitely bookmark those, too. If you simply like free stuff, our Heartopia codes page is a must read before playing.

#4299. Aether Gazer tier list - Jade Forger - Vulu included

Our Aether Gazer tier list is specially created for perfectionists and theory-crafting admins looking for a one-stop guide to deck out your squad fully, or for love-struck admins wishing to bring out the best of their favourites, with so many maidens and blokes clad in exquisite futuristic suits to choose from.

To put an abrupt stop to your dilemma, we have put together an Aether Gazer tier list ranking each Modifier and measuring their overall performance for each part of the game, irrespective of their base ranks. Here’s how it works - each modifier stands a chance to fully realise its potential through Transcendence to the famed Omega rank. In addition, the term Omega is also commonly applied to a combo streak. It is denoted by the letters appearing at the upper left side of the corner that slowly build up as your characters attack.

Now, click on the big blue button, and let's head right into Modifier rankings.

The real-deal elites, regardless of their shape and size, are the premier choice that you should throw your resources at whenever an opportunity arises. They are also the best choices for newbies to grasp the basics. As progression is timed by stamina, I'd encourage you to spend your hard-earned resources on them first. Fret not, as most in this category are obtainable from the starter’s pool.

We're starting off the Aether Gazer tier list with Tyr - he is a self-reliant powerhouse without needing to rely on signature Functors. He works exceptionally well even with a 4-star Functor or lower. His impressive stats provide him with enormous bulk, which can be left comfortably in the hands of AI while being able to dish out excellent damage to bosses and mobs. This is thanks to his skill, which enhances his damage percentage by the thousands (while most Modifiers have a ceiling of hundreds).

Ashura, the petite girl with the appetite of a glutton, is the top-tier fire-element damage dealer, and her position looks set to remain unchallenged for aeons to come. Her most unique calling card lies in her second skill, as she is the only modifier that can trigger a “Zero time” on demand. She is also capable of refreshing her skill cooldown with successful evades. The caveat is that she requires you to be hands-on. The AI simply isn't up to the task. Sakura, the rabbit-crazed maniac, is a top-tier team player as she is blessed with a competitive skill set that brings a plethora of buffs to the table, including a party-wide heal, attack up, pierce, and battery. Just like Tyr, she is already stellar without a signature functor. Her main mechanic as a berserker-type character is rage-inducing - she collects and deals high damage with a pretty important attribute called Divine Grace. Of course, her standout aspect stems from her first skill that randomly grants buffs (purple, yellow and green that bolster self-attack, gain rage points and self-heal). Unlike Rahu Asura, she is one of the best modifiers that has total compatibility with the AI. Artic Abyss is truly the cream of the crop of S rank modifiers - she is a support-oriented modifier who provides ample buffs to the team, and is known (and remains) to be the top-tier battery who provides Cooldown to skills and ultimates for your fellow allies, coupled with some healing and minor power-ups.

They are the second top brass - not the shiniest but their prowess is almost equivalent to the S tier. They are highly capable and robust in their own right. Here is where the majority of A-grade modifiers reside.

Starting this part with, Jin-ei, the one with unrivaled bodysuit appeal, is distinguished by being the jack of all elements and master of none thanks to her skill kit. Each of her skills allows her to deal with different kinds of elemental damage, making her a universal addition to the team. Sher will test enemy’s elemental disadvantages and fits in any element-themed team like a glove.

Moving on in the A rank echelon, we have The Innocence, a modifier shrouded with a meek veneer. Thanks to her damage-oriented kit, she can nearly match everyone here. Additionally, it is easy to max transcend her. Her skills allow her to easily solo bosses and wipe the floor with mobs.

The next A rank modifier is Gusty Lance, an operator who debriefs admins on their missions. She dual-wields combat lances and easily racks up damage by parrying while consistently dodging. On top of that, she easily draws out her strength without relying much on functors, much like Tyr.

Similarly, Frost Fang is an evasion-based modifier just like Gusty Lance. She can receive a good 50% boost to her ice elemental attacks for every successful evasion. She makes for a good boss killer as well as crowd control thanks to the incremental attack gain (up to 90% permanently during battle) granted by one of her skills.

This echelon mostly constitutes A-grade modifiers who fell short compared to the upper ranks, either overshadowed in terms of virtue or their niche involving high stakes. With that said, they can be serviceable to tackle most in-game content with subpar efficiency, provided they are given the proper nourishment.

While their abilities slightly pale in comparison to their peers in higher ranks, they are serviceable and can get through most content, provided they have higher transcendence and better gear investment. This is especially great as the majority of Modifiers here are A-rank modifiers, and so their shards are relatively easier to farm.

Starting with the lone wolf in the bunch, Ryugiri is a base S rank modifier on paper as he is a sturdy tank impervious to hitstun. Due to his expertise in wielding one-handed blades, he is suited to soloing enemy bosses. To achieve maximum efficiency, he requires a boatload of investment (access key functors, transcendence, and sigils) to be able to perform slightly below the strongest S rank modifiers. Above all, he requires the possession of very specific fire-type modifiers, as well as support within a team to fully drive out his potential.

Moving on to the second member of the icy pair, Drifting Flurry is a hybrid support tank modifier. Her standout trait is her skill that can invalidate boss units with crowd control effects that hinder modifiers. She shines perfectly in a full-fledged ice team and pairs well with Vidar.

Shinku is a modifier focused on dealing continuous damage and building up a combo streak. While her blade-slashing animations are flashy and gratifying, she is unfortunately hampered by very low damage output owing to the low damage percentage on all her skills, forcing her to rely on resource investment, particularly Sigils, to function properly. Radiant Feather can ensnare a group of mobs in one spot and apply a debuff that cripples the enemy's resistance to fire-type attacks. She is an ideal support for any fire team, but works exceptionally well with Ryugiri and Aigertlam. Sadly, that’s where her versatility ends. Nuasha stands out as a fire damage dealer with good AoE coverage, but his damage scales with how much damage he consistently takes. Though, as a countermeasure, he can recover a small portion of HP based on the damage he’s taken, branding him as a decent meat shield in a fire team.

This is also known as the "Never-Used" tier.

Just like many other gacha games, each newcomer is given a set of modifiers to unravel their tale. In Aether Gazer, the main “starter” is Verthandi. Her original base variant is less than useful in the long run and should only be used if you find her outspoken and cheerful personality endearing. However, further on in the game, she is poised to receive a new suit that makes her much more viable and feasible in the meta. Still, she can see some use in the early stages thanks to how easily you can stack her character shards for Transcendence.

Other candidates include the tag-along “starter” Surefire and the enigmatic Croc Rage. Surefire, sadly, is overshadowed in every way. Croc Rage, despite his ”hotheaded” banter, is mostly underwhelming with a suicide-happy skillset that takes effort to fully command his character. Some skills are unusable for bosses, though he can dispose of humanoid enemies that can be fulfilled by other modifiers. The sole A rank modifier in this list is The Glare. While his speciality is being able to leap back a distance by repeatedly spamming his second skill, he is hindered by his confusing skill kit and severely low damage output.

And that's our complete Aether Gazer tier list updated with every modifier in the game at the moment. For the latest buzz in the industry, we also have tier lists for NIKKE: Goddess of Victory, Neural Cloud and Path to Nowhere tier list .

#4298. A Mass Effect 5 Trailer Featuring Liara Appears To Have Leaked Following BioWare's Closure

In case you missed the tragic news yesterday, EA laid off 400 employees this week, including all of BioWare. The studio behind Mass Effect, Dragon Age, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and more, has been shut down, and its last remaining project was canceled. The game in question was a fifth entry in the Mass Effect universe, and BioWare shared very little about it – not even an official name. Following the studio's closure, however, a trailer for the sci-fi sequel started circulating around the internet.

While no official BioWare representatives have confirmed that the footage is real, Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier claims that it is. Schreier has a history of credible reporting in the field, and was the first to break the news about the layoffs. IGN has also stated that it confirmed the trailer's legitimacy.

If you want to see for yourself, you can watch the trailer on Reddit.

"The following is in-engine footage form our small team," text at the start of the video reads. "It uses our pre-production assets." The footage shows no gameplay, but includes a good-looking CG cutscene of a new protagonist speaking with an asari woman in a crowded bar. As he tells her about his life, we see glimpses of him as a soldier, then as some kind of spy, traveling to several planets to track down conflicts and "stopping them before they start." After the asari woman reveals that she's been "starting the fires" he's trying to prevent, another woman behind her lowers a hood. This new woman reveals herself as Liara T'Soni, one of Mass Effect's most iconic characters.

Then, Liara and the protagonist team up to take out the woman at the bar and her henchmen, using guns and telekinetic abilities. The trailer fades to black, then fades back in to reveal the game's would-be title: Mass Effect Universe. It's a great-looking trailer – it's a shame the game will never see the light of day.

If you want to join us in grieving BioWare, we republished an oral history of the studio that was originally written by former editor Matt Bertz in 2016. You can also read our cover stories on BioWare's most recent releases: Dragon Age: The Veilguard, Mass Effect: Legendary Edition, Anthem, and Mass Effect Andromeda.

#4297. Invictus Gaming beat Top Esports 3-1 to reach first Worlds semi-final since 2019

Invictus Gaming knocked out fellow LPL side Top Esports in the opening quarter-final of Worlds 2026 in Allen, Texas. The result guarantees China a semi-final place after the LPL's 0-4 start in the Swiss Stage.

Invictus Gaming are through to the last four of Worlds 2026. They beat fellow LPL side Top Esports in the opening match of the Knockout Stage. The series was played at the Credit Union of Texas Event Center in Allen, Texas, on 3 November (US time).

The win guarantees China a semi-final place. That matters after the LPL’s 0-4 start in the Swiss Stage. IG now meet either Gen.G or LYON. Gen.G beat IG 1-0 in the Swiss Stage and finished it with a perfect 3-0 record.

TES played the event without ZUIAN. On 6 October the club announced that Bai ‘369’ Jia-Hao would move into the starting line-up because of visa problems affecting ZUIAN.

The stand-in still made his mark. IG won Game 1 after building a gold lead of more than 10,000. TES levelled in Game 2 when 369, on Renekton, killed JiaQi and TheShy on his own late in the game. IG then took the next two games to close out the series.

Every Knockout Stage match is a single-elimination best-of-five played with Fearless Draft. The two sides knew each other well. They met twice in best-of-five series in September. IG won 3-2 in the LPL Split 3 playoffs on 5 September. TES won 3-1 in the LPL Regional Finals on 17 September.

The prize money gap is now fixed. Worlds 2026 has a total prize pool of US$5,000,000, with US$1,000,000 for the winner. Each losing semi-finalist receives US$400,000, so IG are guaranteed at least that sum.

IG’s run began with a mid-season rescue. The team started LPL Split 3 in the Nirvana Group. The club then asked TheShy and Rookie, who were both on a break, to come back. The pair helped the side qualify for Worlds. Both won the 2018 world title with IG.

TheShy said he had promised IG’s CEO he would help if asked. “I came back to keep my word,” he said after the series.

The #Worlds2026 Knockout Stage bracket after today's match! pic.twitter.com/iaPQndNZSW

— LoL Esports (@lolesports) November 4, 2026

The rest of the quarter-finals follow this week. Gen.G play LYON on 4 November. Dplus KIA face Bilibili Gaming on 5 November. Europe’s last team, Karmine Corp, play T1 on 6 November. All three start at 16:00 CT.

The semi-finals will be played in Allen on 7 and 8 November. The final will be held in Brooklyn on Saturday 14 November at 2pm EST.

#4296. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Review - Silver Bullet

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 arrives at a crossroads for the series, thanks in large part to the inconsistent quality of recent entries. With a shaky predecessor, Infinity Ward had a lot to repair and conclude, especially with 4 set to bookend the rebooted Modern Warfare series. Fortunately, backed up by a fun campaign, thrilling multiplayer, and loads of new modes and content, Modern Warfare 4 makes up for the past and then some.

Modern Warfare 4 continues after the events of 2023’s Modern Warfare 3, with Captain Price hellbent on stopping Makarov and his higher-ups. The story features shifting perspectives, from a new group of ragtag Korean soldiers to familiar characters like Gaz. The character dynamics harken back to the original trilogy, especially in the boots-on-the-ground missions with the South Korean unit, led by Park (played by Beef actor Young Mazino).

For a series that, at least recently, has been more spectacle than story, giving the stakes the time they deserve is nice. While it moves away from the stealthy and modernized elements, it makes sense for the matters at hand. The majority of Modern Warfare 4’s attempts at wrapping up the overarching plot of the rebooted series works, but it rushes through some character arcs and story beats in uneven fashion. Furthermore, much of the game’s cast, especially Mads Mikkelson’s Archer and Prisca Kim’s Ri Ju-Young, are underutilized, which is a shame since they both deliver great performances.

Despite the shortcomings of the campaign, Call of Duty's bread and butter, multiplayer, still delivers. While it doesn’t have the fluidity of Black Ops’ newer entries, the customization and design of weapons and maps make it worth digging into. From small, intimate shooting galleries with Mumbai and Nautical to wide free-for-alls like Coal and Reactor U92, the range helps maintain excitement, even if it gets repetitive over time.

The variety of multiplayer modes keeps things fresh on the battlefield. Returning modes like standard Team Deathmatch and Kill Confirmed continue that enjoyable competitive flair that made them the stars that they are. However, new modes like Combat Outpost and Hijack fit right into the already great lineup. In particular, Combat Outpost upscales your typical 6v6 player count to 24v24, leading to more action and teamwork. Hanging onto a team’s tank, shooting enemies from afar, and taking back outposts is exhilarating, even if it can all go bad moments later by a well-placed RPG shot.

Even after hours of gameplay, the variety of options to craft your perfect gun is impressive. Figuring out the best scope, ammo, stock, and muzzle, as well as the advantages and disadvantages of them, is a fun way of customizing your playstyle. Gunny, a mechanic that helps optimize your gun for certain styles, can help with decision paralysis, but I rarely used it. Not many FPSs go that far and Modern Warfare 4’s commitment to the feature makes it stand out.

The newest mode, DMZ, impresses out of the gate. After a few flat attempts in the past, this is the definitive Call of Duty extraction shooter, whether you play solo, or in duos or trios. Immediately, you’re thrust into the wide open world of Hajin and left to fend for yourselves with what you have and what you can gather and extract. Fans of Arc Raiders and Marathon should feel right at home as the gameplay borrows from the typical extraction shooter experience. Intense, action-packed moments keep you coming back after every win or loss. And the excellent gunplay and level design elevate it into something worthwhile, no matter how you play.

Despite not encountering many live players during my time in Hajin in DMZ, it still proves challenging, even for seasoned pros. The world is not your friend, and taking risks can come at a high cost. A good team, as well as a thoughtful loadout and traits, are required to survive. The unpredictability of it all keeps you on your toes, making for an exciting addition to the already strong multiplayer suite.

Regardless of the mode, Modern Warfare 4 is one of the best-looking Call of Duty titles to date. New York and Paris are lifelike, and it truly embodies the realistic, modern aesthetic the series has always aimed to achieve. However, I encountered a few technical hiccups, especially in the campaign. Slow framerate plagues some high-octane scenes and texture loading is frequent across the board. These distractions are far from game-breaking, but enough to be noticeable.

While the plot execution is a bit shaky, engaging multiplayer options, including DMZ, aptly demonstrate that Infinity Ward can still deliver compelling military-FPS experiences. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is a strong return to form that serves as a solid sendoff for the rebooted subseries.

#4295. Roblox: Elemental Dungeons tier list - The Best (and worst) elements

An up-to-date Elemental Dungeons tier list after Update 9

Thanks to an ever-changing meta, creating an Elemental Dungeons tier list isn’t as easy as it is for most Roblox experiences. New elements get added regularly, and old ones are dumped into oblivion. On top of all that, elements getting nerfed or buffed in an update is quite common. While no one likes this much uncertainty surrounding one of the most important aspects of the game, it is what it is. Those who love crawling through the elemental dungeons have already made peace with it. So, it’s about time someone made an Elemental Dungeons elements tier list and kept it updated. Elemental Dungeons tier list explained After the latest update, there are 15 elements in Elemental Dungeons. We've ranked them into five different tiers, from tier S to tier D. The S tier is the strongest, while the D tier is for the weakest elements.

Check out our Elemental Dungeons guide for beginners to learn more about the Elements and how to use them. Our guide tells you how to obtain the Elements, use them effectively and get the best out of them. This tier list also tells you which elements are worth obtaining and upgrading.

With a new max mastery of 250, Angel has recently jumped from Epic to Legendary rarity. It is strong against Reaper, among others, and only weak against Lightning and Lava. It can deal massive AoE damage and heal nearby allies.

When an element is strong against EIGHT of the fifteen total elements, A tier is the least it deserves. Lightning is an Epic element that has been nerfed, nerfed, and nerfed, and yet still seems OP somehow. If it wasn’t for the nerfs, Lightning could have been in the S tier, but it still gives the Mythic and Legendary elements a run for their money. The damage-dealing abilities of this element are insane. Lightning is capable of destroying anything the game throws at you.

Light is an Epic tier element that was added to Elemental Dungeons with Update 1. It has 300 max mastery, and much like other elements, Light also has FIVE abilities. However, what sets Light apart is the fact that its third ability, Light Ray, and ultimate, Light Barrage, cast 16 ticks of damage while dealing three and four-figure damage per tick, respectively. Light is a decent substitute if you can’t get your hands on a Mythic element.

Ice is exactly what you’d expect from an Epic element. It does plenty of damage, but it is not overpowered. Ice can fight and destroy anyone and anything, but it’s hard work. Unlike the Mythic elements, you can’t one-shot anyone with Ice. But that doesn’t make it a bad element. Once you reach a good enough mastery level, you can spam an Ice Barrage and Ice Shuriken combo to deal massive damage that goes as high as 10,000+.

Although it is Legendary, Gravity doesn’t really belong in the Legendary tier. While I won’t tag it as the weakest Legendary element, it’s certainly not the strongest. The damage it deals is mediocre at best, but a couple of things are OP, which saved Gravity from falling to C tier. First is the seemingly unlimited range of the second skill, Meteor, and the second is the low cooldowns. Almost all of Gravity's skills become available within 5-10 seconds.

I’ll just say it. Air is a bad Rare element that’s pretty easy to get early. However, you should forget about it as soon as you get it. Fighting enemies with Air is hard, and fighting boss battles is even harder. The attacks are all over the place and miss the target half of the time. It’s only strong against elements that are weaker than Air.

Low damage, high AoE, strong against SIX elements but weak against SEVEN, Water is a weird element and not in a good way. Water is the only element whose strongest ability is the first. As you unlock Mastery Skills 2 and 3, the attack stats get lower and lower. It’s just not worth building on unless you’re really bored and are looking for a challenge.

That’s it for my Elemental Dungeons tier list. As the meta changes, which it surely will, I’ll make sure to update this tier list accordingly. Until then, have fun and keep an eye on similar content like ourAnime Dimensions tier list, thisBlade Ball ability tier list or ourUltimate Tower Defense tier list, to name a few that stand out.

#4294. Epic Adds Features to Fortnite Crew Subscription, Removes Others

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

Fortnite’s self-perpetuating freemium economy is built around several forms of transactions and subscriptions. The most prominent of these are the Item Shop, where you buy cosmetics piecemeal for V-Bucks, and the Battle Pass, which you buy once per season to gain access to a set sequence of unlockables by leveling up.

In addition to these, though, Fortnite also offers the Fortnite Crew subscription service which, for a recurring monthly fee, gets you access to the current Battle Pass, other content passes like the OG Pass, Music Pass, and for fans of video game LEGO kits, the LEGO Pass, plus a monthly payout of 800 V-Bucks. It costs more than the Battle Pass by itself, but all the extra content is very attractive, especially if you don’t already have a bunch of skins to flip through.

During the Treasure Hunters event, players have a chance to uncover a token that gives near-unfettered access to the item shop for two weeks.

As Epic Games announced on the official Fortnite news blog today, though, some changes are coming to the Crew Subscription starting on December 5. Some of these changes are additive, and may help to improve the value of the subscription gameplay-wise, but they’re accompanied by some subtractions, which could harm the overall bang-for-buck depending on your perspective.

Let’s start with the good news. Firstly, the price of Fortnite Crew is staying the same at $11.99 monthly, and you’ll still get access to the current Battle Pass, Music Pass, LEGO Pass and Rocket Pass Premium.

The price of Fortnite Crew is staying the same at $11.99 monthly.

The people gave Sweeney and Epic all the attention and support it needed when it rose up to Apple. As a reward, players got a significant price hike.

In addition, all Crew members will begin receiving a flat 20% bonus to all XP earned while playing the game, with a 10% XP bonus also given to any squad members in your party, even if they’re not Crew members themselves. These boosts don’t stack, though, so you won’t get any additional XP even if you have other Crew members in your squad.

So, that’s the good news, now what’s the bad news? The first piece of bad news is that Crew Pack Outfits, one of the most distinctive benefits to getting a Crew sub, are being discontinued. The final Crew Pack Outfit will be distributed in December, with no further packs to follow. On the bright side, if there were any Legacy Styles you didn’t have for your Crew Pack Outfits, which would normally be obtained by staying subbed for sequential months, they’ll instead just be given to you in bulk.

The second piece of bad news is that, at least for the time being, OG Pass is ending, with an apparent “dramatic conclusion” occurring on December 5 with the end of Chapter 1: OG Season X. This means you won’t be able to redeem the large quantity of skins and other assorted cosmetics that this pass would normally provide.

That’s definitely a big blow to the overall value factor of a Crew subscription, though according to Epic’s news post, “The Next Era of Fortnite OG drops in late 2027,” so perhaps the OG Pass will make a comeback at some point.

Epic Games has laid off over 1,000 employees and cut three game modes from Fortnite, raising questions about the company's (and Fortnite's) future.

#4293. Gen.G sweep LYON to end North America’s Worlds 2026 run and set up iG semi-final

Gen.G beat LYON 3-0 in Allen, Texas, removing North America's last team from Worlds 2026. The LCK top seed are now one series from a first Worlds final, with a revived Invictus Gaming in the way.

Gen.G swept LYON in the second Worlds 2026 quarter-final in Allen, Texas. The defeat removes North America’s last team from the tournament. The LCK top seed now face Invictus Gaming in a best-of-five semi-final on Saturday, starting at 16:00 Central Time.

Gen.G went into the series with the better record. That gave them first choice of side for game one, and they picked blue. They stayed on blue side for games two and three.

Reaching the last four secures Gen.G at least third or fourth place. That is a familiar stopping point for the organisation. It has finished third or fourth at four of its last five Worlds and has never played in a Worlds final, GosuGamers reported.

The stakes go beyond one team. Gen.G entered the tournament as the LCK’s top seed. Korean sides are chasing a fifth Summoner’s Cup in a row.

Their opponents bring their own history. Invictus Gaming beat Top Esports 3-1 in the opening quarter-final. That put iG into their first Worlds semi-final since 2019. TheShy and Rookie, who won Worlds with iG in 2018, are back in the last four.

The money rises sharply from here. Worlds 2026 carries a US$5,000,000 prize pool. The champion takes US$1,000,000 (20%), and the runner-up receives US$800,000.

For LYON, the exit still marks clear progress. They go out in joint fifth to eighth place and collect a share of the prize money. GosuGamers called it easily the organisation’s best Worlds finish. In four earlier appearances, LYON never placed higher than 17th.

Their elimination also changes the shape of the event. North America will have no representative in the semi-finals or the Grand Final. The remaining matches in Allen will be contested without a team from the region.

LYON are eliminated from #Worlds2026. pic.twitter.com/y5cWOL9e5K

— LoL Esports (@lolesports) November 5, 2026

The Grand Final is listed for 14:00 EST on 14 November. British fans will have a dedicated place to watch it. The British Esports Federation is holding a watch party at the new British Arena in Sunderland. It is the venue’s first esports watch party.

The arena covers 15,000 sq ft. It has a 17-metre-wide LED screen, a 200-seat viewing area and a bar. Students can get discounted tickets.

Whether Gen.G or iG make it to that final will be settled in Allen on Saturday. The Sunderland watch party runs from 5:30pm on the day of the final until 1:00am on 15 November.

#4292. Amazon’s Mass Effect TV Series Is Reportedly Still In Production Despite BioWare Closure

EA shut down legendary RPG developer BioWare this week, canceling its in-development fifth Mass Effect game as a result. Despite the closure, Amazon Prime’s upcoming Mass Effect streaming series will proceed as planned, according to a report by IGN.

Amazon MGM Studios began developing a Mass Effect series in 2024. At the time, Mass Effect series executive producer Mike Gamble confirmed the show isn't a retelling of the video games, saying, “The show will explore a brand-new story within the universe's timeline, and will be set after the original trilogy. It won't be a retread of Commander Shepard's story – because after all... that's YOUR story, isn’t it?”

With BioWare’s closure, one would think the series would go up in smoke, but sources within Prime Video speaking to IGN confirmed that it remains in development. Furthermore, all of the creatives involved remain so. This includes showrunners Doug Jung (The Cloverfield Paradox, Star Trek Beyond) and Daniel Casey (F9: The Fast Saga, Wardriver), former Marvel Studios head Avi Arad, and Jessica Jones executive producer Karim Zreik. Mike Gamble was also involved, and this report suggests he still is, but it remains to be seen how his position on the project has changed with BioWare’s demise, given he served as a guiding voice from the studio. The Mass Effect series has no release window.

The Mass Effect series joins other video game adaptations Amazon has in the works, which include a third season of Fallout (with Aaron Paul joining the cast), a live-action God of War series starring Dave Bautista, a live-action Tomb Raider series starring Sophie Turner, as well as series based on Life is Strange and Wolfenstein.

For more on Mass Effect, check out our review of the Legendary Edition and our recently republished Oral History of BioWare from 2016.

Explore everything Talos-II has to offer with the best squad from our definitive Arknights Endfield Tier List!

Thanks to the wealth of content within this gorgeous RPG, an Arknights Endfield tier list simply can't contain them all. There are so many ways you can combine characters and combo their skills that you just can't rank them all in the S-tier and call it a day (although that would be nice, wouldn't it?).

Now, I've written this piece slightly differently from my other ones, as I've decided it would be best to divide them by roles, as well as elements.

I know - it's a lot to take in at first glance, but since there are not realistically "bad" characters, that's the only logical conclusion I could reach. Even if a character is not 6*, it can still be exceptional when teamed up with another. It's all about synergy. Some characters, of course, cannot be compared - we can't put a DPS next to a support and rank them.

Oh, and if you're only just starting out, we've also got a handy Arknights Endfield beginner's guide to lend you a hand. It's not always easy to get the hang of things right away, but hopefully we can help give you a headstart!

In any case, if you want to know how well each one of the Operators ranks, let's dive in - and for something even more in-depth, we've also got a character guide for every single one!
